method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, exact formula and macro replay, and reverse paraphrase of the theorem and computation-code explanation. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Kleene's Normal Form Theorem, universal primitive recursive T and U, and the index/computation-code explanation.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: There are fixed primitive recursive T and U such that every partial recursive f has at least one index e and, for every x, f(x) is partially equal to U of the least s satisfying T(e,x,s).
samples.checks: The universal functions and relation, existential placement of e, every-x quantification, partial equality and mu-search formula retain their source scope.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An index codes a program or definition; a terminating computation has a number code s whose validity and output are primitive recursively checkable. One unbounded search suffices, and every partial recursive function has infinitely many indices.
samples.checks: Definedness, code checking, extraction of the result and infinitely-many-indices claim are preserved without treating the program index as an input value.

limitations: MR-P154 directly attests the normal-form phrase, not Kleene's full theorem title; MR-P155 attests index in another technical domain, while OpenLogic defines this use.
No TeX reader build was run for this source-only unit checkpoint.
